human_authorisation.authorisation_note: User asked the product to grow comparable features to other coaching apps, bounded by the repo's own guidelines, and approved a 4-feature plan (progress photos, body metrics/habits, exercise reference media, device sync) with the explicit caveat that exercise reference media should be infrastructure-only since there is no video content to populate yet. This slice is that infrastructure step: an optional reference_media field added to the exercise registry's schema, following the S-REG-32 precedent of a schema-only extension bundled outside the S-REG-23/24 activation authority. The field stays unset on all 19 live entries in this slice; a separate ordinary product-facing surface (FULL-UI-30) exposes it read-only, always returning null until a later slice adds real content.

rollback_plan.primary: git revert <this-slice-commit> - reverses the 3 exercise schema files and this slice's own scaffolding atomically back to the pre-extension state in one step. No registry data, bundle, or seal file is touched by this slice, so no other rollback step is needed.
rollback_plan.fallback: If a clean revert is not possible: remove the reference_media property block from ci/schemas/exercise.registry.schema.json, ci/schemas/exercise.registry.schema.v1.0.0.json, and ci/schemas/exercise_registry.schema.json, confirming all 3 files return to the pre-extension hashes recorded in schema_file_hashes_before. No bundle regeneration or seal re-pin is required since neither was touched.

runtime_parity_proof.note: This slice touches only ci/schemas/ files, which the engine's exercise loader (engine/src/registries/loadExerciseEntries.ts) never reads - it parses registries/exercise/exercise.registry.json directly with no schema/ajv validation step. Since exercise.registry.json's content and registry_index.json's order[] are both completely untouched, PHASE_3's loaded_registries list cannot be affected. All 13 e2e:golden fixtures were captured before this slice and re-captured after every mutation in this slice; all 13 were byte-identical. This was verified directly, not assumed.
